newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Exiled Cambodian prince plans to return home.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Cambodian prince plans to return home.

text.p: Cambodia's Prince Norodom Sirivudh, exiled last year for allegedly plotting to kill one of the country's two premiers, has said he plans to return home soon despite the dangers he could face.

"My decision is taken. What do I risk? Prison, surveillance of my home, death perhaps? But I prefer to die in Cambodia," the prince told the Cambodge Soir newspaper in an interview conducted in Paris and published on Monday evening.

"I had promised the king (his half-brother Norodom Sihanouk) to leave for one year to calm people down. I have kept my promise, I want to return to work in the reconstruction of my country," Sirivudh said, giving no return date.
Sirivudh also maintained that he had no interest in succeeding the ailing Sihanouk, who recently turned 74, and supported a constitutional change to allow a queen to reign.
Sihanouk has said, however, his wife Monineath has no ambitions for the throne.

The prince, a former foreign minister who has denied any involvement in the alleged assassination plot against Hun Sen, was allowed to leave for French exile last December following the intervention of the king and after a month of detention.
A Phnom Penh court later sentenced him in absentia to 10 years imprisonment on charges linked to the plot, although diplomats and foreign rights workers dismissed the trial as a sham.

Sihanouk in September granted an amnesty to dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary from an earlier death sentence for his role in the crimes against humanity perpetrated by the 1975-79 Khmer Rouge regime, prompting calls for Sirivudh's pardon.
Sirivudh also wrote to the the king last month seeking his approval and help to return home.
First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh has also said he would support the return of Sirivudh, his former right-hand man in the royalist FUNCINPEC party.
Hun Sen remains the key to an amnesty, however, and so far he has not given his blessing for the return of a man he sees as one of his main political enemies.
"I am returning without a spirit of vengeance, more with the idea of working in the national consensus," Sirivudh was quoted as saying.
